tradition_rules.orthodox: Legacy tag, the same books as eastern_orthodox. Kept until Alpha approves removing it (ROADMAP item 3).
tradition_rules.eastern_orthodox: Books the Eastern Orthodox (Greek and Slavonic) churches read as scripture [orthodoxwiki].
tradition_rules.oriental_orthodox: Only books all six Oriental Orthodox churches (Coptic, Syriac, Armenian, Ethiopian, Eritrean, Malankara) read as scripture (Alpha, 2026-10-18). Each book cites a source per church; a book any church is unconfirmed for is marked NEEDS REVIEW and left out. The Eritrean church is taken to keep the Ethiopian canon it shares, and the Malankara church the Syriac (Peshitta) canon; both to be confirmed in the pre-launch review (NEEDS_APPROVAL #5).
tradition_rules.ethiopian_orthodox: Books the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church reads as scripture [tewahedo].

references.coptic: Coptic Orthodox Diocese of Los Angeles, 'The Deuterocanonical Books': Tobit, Judith, Sequel of Esther, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, Sequel of Daniel, 1 and 2 Maccabees, Psalm 151. https://www.lacopts.org/orthodoxy/our-faith/the-holy-bible/the-deuterocanonical-books/
references.tewahedo: Wikipedia, 'Orthodox Tewahedo biblical canon': the whole Catholic deuterocanon except 1 and 2 Maccabees (the Meqabyan are different books); the Prayer of Manasseh within 2 Chronicles. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthodox_Tewahedo_biblical_canon
references.armenian: Armenian Church Library: the Armenian Apostolic Church recognises the deuterocanonical books as scripture (Wisdom, Tobit, Judith, 1 and 2 Maccabees named). https://www.armenianchurchlibrary.com/AmericanStandardVersion.html
references.peshitta: Encyclopedia.pub, 'Peshitta': the Leiden base text has the Hebrew Bible books plus Wisdom, Letter of Jeremiah, Baruch, Bel and the Dragon, Susanna, Judith, Sirach, 1-4 Maccabees. https://encyclopedia.pub/entry/28378
references.peshitta-nt: Syriac Orthodox Resources, 'The Peshitto': the Peshitta New Testament lacks 2 Peter, 2 and 3 John, Jude and Revelation, which are still not read in Syriac churches. https://syriacorthodoxresources.org/Bible/Peshitto.html
references.chart: Bombaxo, 'Comparison Chart of the Historically Held Biblical Canons' (Syrian, Coptic, Ethiopian and Armenian columns). https://www.bombaxo.com/biblical-canon/comparison-chart-of-the-historically-held-canons-of-different-churches/
references.psalm151: Wikipedia, 'Psalm 151': accepted as canonical by the Eastern Orthodox and Oriental Orthodox churches. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psalm_151
references.orthodoxwiki: OrthodoxWiki, 'Deuterocanon': the Eastern Orthodox Old Testament adds 1 Esdras, Tobit, Judith, Wisdom, Sirach, Baruch, Letter of Jeremiah, the additions to Daniel and Esther, 1-3 Maccabees, the Prayer of Manasseh and Psalm 151 (4 Maccabees in an appendix). https://orthodoxwiki.org/Deuterocanon
